Verdict: ACCEPTI accept the new neutral U-port turning theorem and its shared-budget consequences as ordinary mathematical results under the stated complete-source assumptions and the accepted dependencies. The polygon construction survives arbitrary additional contacts and the two-source parallel-edge case. The contact signs, cyclic reindexing, both counting inequalities, and the occurrence inclusion  $B_{10}\le B$  are correct.The AA consequence is also valid inside the same endpoint component satisfying the accepted AA hypotheses. Section 5 should explicitly restrict its globally introduced count symbols to that component. This is consistent with its stated “same-component AA residual” setting; extending  $B_{10}=0$  to unrelated components would be invalid.There is no execution certification in this verdict. The displayed Lean statements are conditional, and the physical, planar, and AA adapters remain written. The checker also does not explicitly reconstruct the occurrence inclusion  $B_{10}\subseteq B$ , although that inclusion has a valid direct proof.Below, “neutral note,” “passive-corner note,” and “reserve note” refer to the three supplied documents.1. The specified graph really produces simple polygons1.1 The relevant graph is a multigraph on original ownersAn eligible original U owner contributes exactly its two specified ports. A neutral contact pairs two ports belonging to distinct original owners. Its physical tile has precisely two endpoints, so a given port has at most one partner.Consequently, a closed connected component is a finite, connected, loopless, 2-regular multigraph. It has a cyclic traversal that visits each original owner once and each neutral edge once. If it has  $n$  owners, it has  $n$  edges, counted with multiplicity.This includes a component with two owners joined by two edges. The two edges use different ports of each owner; they are distinct contacts, even though they have the same pair of owner vertices. Nothing here permits a self-loop or identifies those two contacts. These facts follow from the graph definition in the neutral note, §1.1.2 Substituting the source arcs preserves distinct verticesFor a phase01 owner, expand the chosen route into unit lattice steps along:
$$\text{first terminal}\longrightarrow
\text{first stem}\longrightarrow
\text{outer bar}\longrightarrow
\text{second stem}\longrightarrow
\text{second terminal}.$$
In normalized coordinates this is the path through
$$(h_L,1),\ldots,(0,1),(0,2),\ldots,(0,v),
(1,v),\ldots,(h_R,v).$$
The two stems occupy different columns, and their only intersections with the bar are their respective bar corners. Thus the path is simple. Independent positive stem heights change its lengths without introducing an intersection.For a phase10 owner, the chosen arc is the straight outer-bar row, again expanded into unit steps.Every vertex of either arc is an original endpoint of that owner. Therefore:Different owners’ arcs have disjoint vertex sets, by original endpoint disjointness.Each arc has no repeated vertex.The component traversal uses each owner’s arc once.Each contact attaches to an endpoint of an arc, and each port participates in exactly one contact.After concatenation, the polygon has a cyclic list of distinct lattice vertices, with only the final return identifying the starting vertex. This is the essential bridge between the abstract owner cycle and the geometric curve. It uses the unchanged original endpoint sets, not any assumption that the full contact graph has degree two. [Neutral note, §§1 and 3; port_data.]1.3 There are no hidden edge crossingsDistinct vertices alone would not establish simplicity for arbitrary straight-line drawings. Here the unit square-lattice geometry supplies the additional fact.A unit horizontal or vertical lattice segment has no lattice point in its interior. A horizontal lattice edge and a vertical lattice edge can intersect only at integer coordinates. For unit edges, such an intersection must therefore be an endpoint of both.Collinear unit edges overlap only if they coincide. Coincidence is excluded as follows:Two source edges from different owners cannot coincide because their endpoint sets are disjoint.A contact edge cannot coincide with a source edge: the contact’s endpoints have different original owners, whereas a source edge’s endpoints have the same owner.Two distinct contact edges cannot coincide without reusing their ports.There is also no immediate reversal at a polygon vertex: with unit steps, that would repeat the preceding vertex.Thus the concatenated curve is a simple closed lattice polygon. Straight intermediate vertices can be suppressed when applying the orthogonal-polygon turning theorem.1.4 Additional contacts and parallel edges do not invalidate this argumentAdditional contacts: An unused endpoint adjacency may be a chord of the chosen polygon, an external adjacency, or a connection to another specified closed component. It does not add an edge to the chosen curve or make its traversal repeat a vertex. The curve need not be an induced cycle of the full contact graph.Parallel owner edges: In a two-owner component, substituting the two source arcs gives two vertex-disjoint paths joined at their endpoints by two distinct unit contacts. This is a polygon, not a geometric two-edge loop with coincident sides.Accordingly, neither concern creates a simplicity gap. A useful clarification in §3 would be:A cyclic traversal of the connected loopless 2-regular multigraph visits each original owner once; after substituting its source arc, all polygon vertices are distinct.The existing argument supports this statement.2. The source and contact signs are correct2.1 Source turnsAt a port  $p$ , let  $s$  point from  $p$  into the chosen source arc, and let  $d$  point toward its original adjacent blank. The original support is  $p-s$ , and
$$\chi=\det(s,d)\in\{-1,1\}.$$
For phase01, one can use Cartesian coordinates in which the source arc runs from the left terminal down its stem, across the bar, and up the right stem. The terminal blanks face into the gap:
$$s_L=s_R=(0,-1),\qquad
d_L=(1,0),\qquad d_R=(-1,0).$$
Hence
$$\chi_L=1,\qquad \chi_R=-1.$$
The left-to-right arc makes two positive quarter-turns, so its internal turn is
$$2=-2\chi_R.$$
Reversing the traversal changes both the exit port and the turn sign, preserving the formula
$$\text{phase01 source turn}=-2\chi_{\rm exit}.$$
For phase10, the chosen bar is straight. Its inward directions at the two ends are opposite, and its two blank directions point to the same side of the bar. Its port chiralities are therefore opposite, and its internal turn is zero.Translations and rotations preserve these relations. Reflections reverse determinants and signed turns together. Unequal stem heights do not enter the sign calculation. The fixed physical partition must remain transported as stipulated; the proof does not introduce a new partition during normalization. [Neutral note, §3; passive-corner note, model assumptions.]2.2 Active-to-passive contact frameLet  $p$  be active and  $q$  passive. Since the active port’s original blank is the other endpoint,
$$q=p+d_p.$$
Since the passive port’s original support is  $p$ ,
$$p=q-s_q,$$
which gives
$$s_q=d_p.$$
The four physical tile corners are
$$p,\qquad p+d_p,\qquad p-s_p,\qquad p+d_p-s_p.$$
The other adjacent tile corner at  $q$  is its blank. Consequently,
$$d_q=-s_p.$$
It follows that
$$\chi_q
=\det(s_q,d_q)
=\det(d_p,-s_p)
=\det(s_p,d_p)
=\chi_p.$$
Thus chirality is preserved across a contact in either traversal direction.2.3 Contact turns include both incident port verticesThe contact contribution must include the turn at the current source’s exit and the turn at the next source’s entry. With that convention:Current exitTurn at the exitTurn at the next entryTotal contact contributionActive $-\chi$  $0$  $-\chi$ Passive $0$  $+\chi$  $+\chi$ For an active exit, the incoming source tangent is  $-s_p$ , the contact tangent is  $d_p$ , and the next source begins in direction  $s_q=d_p$ . The only turn is
$$\det(-s_p,d_p)=-\chi_p.$$
For a passive exit, the contact continues straight in direction  $-s_p$ . The reversed contact frame gives the next source direction  $-d_p$ , so the entry turn is
$$\det(-s_p,-d_p)=\chi_p.$$
Therefore, with  $\beta_i=1$  for an active exit and  $\beta_i=-1$  for a passive exit, the measured contact turn is precisely
$$-\chi_i\beta_i.$$
Every polygon vertex is either an interior source-arc vertex or one of these port vertices, so this decomposition neither omits nor repeats a turn.Combining source and contact contributions gives measured polygon turn
$$-\sum_i\chi_i(2u_i+\beta_i)=-T.$$
The simple orthogonal polygon has total signed quarter-turns  $+4$  or  $-4$ , proving
$$T\in\{-4,4\}.$$
The sign convention in equation (4) is consistent.3. Alternation and cyclic reindexing are validContact chirality is preserved, while the two ports of each source have opposite chirality. Therefore consecutive exit chiralities satisfy
$$\chi_{i+1}=-\chi_i.$$
Closing the cycle forces an even number of owners and gives
$$\sum_i\chi_i=0.$$
Now let  $a_i$  be the number of active neutral ports of owner  $i$ . These  $a_i$  are port-orientation counts; they are not the positive singleton activations counted by the budget variable  $A$ .The exit of owner  $i$  is active with indicator  $(1+\beta_i)/2$ . Its entry is active precisely when the preceding exit is passive. Thus
$$a_i
=\frac{1+\beta_i}{2}+\frac{1-\beta_{i-1}}2
=1+\frac{\beta_i-\beta_{i-1}}2.$$
The decisive cyclic reindexing is
$$\sum_i\chi_i\beta_{i-1}
=\sum_j\chi_{j+1}\beta_j
=-\sum_j\chi_j\beta_j.$$
Consequently,
$$\begin{aligned}
\sum_i\chi_i a_i
&=\sum_i\chi_i
+\frac12\sum_i\chi_i\beta_i
-\frac12\sum_i\chi_i\beta_{i-1}\\
&=\sum_i\chi_i\beta_i.
\end{aligned}$$
Starting from the geometric turn formula,
$$\begin{aligned}
T
&=2\sum_{01}\chi_i+\sum_i\chi_i a_i\\
&=\sum_{01}\chi_i a_i
  +\sum_{10}\chi_i(a_i-2),
\end{aligned}$$
where the last equality uses
$$\sum_{01}\chi_i=-\sum_{10}\chi_i.$$
Equation (5) therefore follows from the geometry. The phase10 correction has the stated sign and coefficient; it is not an extra assumption introduced during the counting argument.4. Both count inequalities follow4.1 First inequalityFix one closed component. Write
$$A_{01}^{\rm port}=\sum_{01}a_i,\qquad
A_{10}^{\rm port}=\sum_{10}a_i.$$
There is exactly one active port on each edge, and the component has one edge per owner. This remains true for parallel edges counted with multiplicity. Hence
$$A_{01}^{\rm port}+A_{10}^{\rm port}=m_{01}+m_{10}.$$
There are  $2m_{10}$  phase10 ports altogether, of which  $b_{10}$  are passive, so
$$A_{10}^{\rm port}=2m_{10}-b_{10},
\qquad
A_{01}^{\rm port}=m_{01}-m_{10}+b_{10}.$$
Since  $0\le a_i\le2$ , equation (5) yields
$$\begin{aligned}
4=|T|
&\le\sum_{01}a_i+\sum_{10}(2-a_i)\\
&=A_{01}^{\rm port}+b_{10}\\
&=m_{01}-m_{10}+2b_{10}.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus
$$4+m_{10}\le m_{01}+2b_{10}.$$
The signed difference  $m_{01}-m_{10}$  causes no problem: the expression to which it is equated is the nonnegative capacity  $A_{01}^{\rm port}+b_{10}$ .4.2 Second inequalitySubtracting the zero sum  $\sum_i\chi_i$  from equation (5) gives
$$T=\sum_{01}\chi_i(a_i-1)
  +\sum_{10}\chi_i(a_i-3).$$
The corresponding absolute local weights are:Active ports  $a_i$ Phase01 weight  $\lvert a_i-1\rvert$ Phase10 weight  $\lvert a_i-3\rvert$ 013102211With the note’s notation for double-active, double-passive, and single-active owners,
$$4\le p_{01}+q_{01}+p_{10}+3q_{10}+2t_{10}.$$
Total active-port balance says that the number of double-active owners equals the number of double-passive owners:
$$p_{01}+p_{10}=q_{01}+q_{10}.$$
Also,
$$b_{10}=2q_{10}+t_{10}.$$
Therefore,
$$\begin{aligned}
4
&\le (p_{01}+p_{10})+q_{01}+3q_{10}+2t_{10}\\
&=2q_{01}+4q_{10}+2t_{10}\\
&=2(q_{01}+b_{10}),
\end{aligned}$$
proving
$$2\le q_{01}+b_{10}.$$
Summing the two inequalities over the closed components gives exactly
$$\boxed{4\ell+M_{10}\le M_{01}+2B_{10}},
\qquad
\boxed{2\ell\le Q_{01}+B_{10}}.$$
Each polygon’s absolute turn is taken before summation. Opposite orientations or nested polygons therefore do not cause cancellation.The reported opposed-band count pattern
$$m_{01}=m_{10}=1,\qquad b_{10}=2,\qquad q_{01}=0$$
attains both numerical inequalities. In fact, for a two-owner cycle the inequalities and active balance force this phase pattern: the phase01 owner is double-active and the phase10 owner double-passive. This checks consistency with the reported control class without certifying its execution.5. Original-owner nonreuse and  $B_{10}\hookrightarrow B$ 5.1 Nonreuse is valid for the specified graphUse the original occurrence identity
$$(o,j),$$
where  $o$  is an original owner and  $j$  identifies one of its two specified ports.Connected components of the specified graph partition its owner vertices. Thus:An original owner contributes to at most one specified closed component.Either of its ports contributes to at most one such component.Reversing a traversal changes entry and exit roles, not the original occurrence identity.Additional contacts may put several specified closed components into one full endpoint component. They do not alter this partition of the specified graph.This establishes the required nonreuse for  $M_{01},M_{10},Q_{01}$ , and  $B_{10}$ . It does not establish a general nonreuse theorem for all other gate or positive-side witnesses involving these owners. The note does not need such a stronger assertion.5.2 Every counted passive10 port satisfies the actual definition of  $B$ The inclusion is direct:Predicate defining an occurrence counted by  $B$ Why a closed passive phase10 port satisfies itOriginal phase10 U outer-corner singletonThese are precisely the phase10 ports selected in §1Actual receiver is nonfull  $2P1T$ Required by the neutral-edge definitionOriginal support is consumedThe passive port’s support is the other endpointOriginal blank is not an endpointThe blank is outside  $P$  in the passive orientationThese are the predicates in the passive-corner note, §1. No conversion to a joint event pool, activation count, or newly chosen witness is involved.Formally, map a counted closed-port occurrence to its original corner:
$$\iota:(\text{closed component},o,j)\longmapsto(o,j).$$
If two inputs have the same image, they have the same owner and original corner. Since an owner belongs to only one specified component, the inputs coincide. Thus  $\iota$  is injective, and
$$\boxed{B_{10}\le B}.$$
An owner with two counted passive corners contributes two distinct original corner occurrences to both sides. There is no illicit replacement of corner counts by owner counts.5.3 The budget’s source collection must remain appropriateBecause a specified closed component need not be a full endpoint component, a passive corner’s route in the accepted theorem may reach a positive activation or defect outside that curve.The budget is therefore taken over the same full source collection—or an appropriately justified full endpoint component—as in the accepted passive-corner theorem. It is not automatically a budget restricted to the phase01/phase10 owners lying on one curve.The neutral note’s instruction that counts use the same source collection as the budget is necessary and correctly placed.6. The shared-budget substitution does avoid double countingThe valid sequence is:Count original curve owners and passive corners without repetition.Aggregate over the specified closed components.Apply the identity inclusion  $B_{10}\le B$ .Apply the single accepted inequality
$$B\le2A+H.$$
This proves the conjunction
$$4\ell+M_{10}\le M_{01}+4A+2H,$$

$$2\ell\le Q_{01}+2A+H.$$
The coefficient  $4A$  in the first inequality comes from substituting into the already present term  $2B_{10}$ . It does not assert that the original charging theorem supplies four separate claims per activation.The accepted possibility that one activated positive leg receives a corner claim and a terminal claim remains represented by the factor two in
$$B\le2A+H.$$
This possibility may occur across different specified curve components. Aggregating the distinct  $B_{10}$  occurrences first and then using the global  $B$  bound preserves that shared capacity.A precise expression of the simultaneous requirement is
$$2A+H\ge
\max\!\left\{
0,\,
\left\lceil\frac{4\ell+M_{10}-M_{01}}2\right\rceil,\,
2\ell-Q_{01}
\right\}.$$
The argument does not replace this maximum by the sum of the two positive deficits.Reserve substitutionThe reserve note supplies
$$2R=A+U_0+Z_0+H.$$
Hence
$$4A+2H=8R-4U_0-4Z_0-2H.$$
Substitution gives precisely
$$\boxed{
4\ell+M_{10}+2H+4U_0+4Z_0
\le M_{01}+8R
}.$$
For completeness, the second shared inequality can likewise be rewritten as
$$2\ell+H+2U_0+2Z_0\le Q_{01}+4R.$$
Both are algebraic consequences using the same reserve identity. Neither creates an additional reserve payment.In particular, the passive-corner note explicitly leaves the direct  $D$  stops unproved disjoint from some older irregular-pair witnesses. This new substitution does not need that missing disjointness. Adding its reserve requirement to an unrelated  $E_{\rm pair}$  requirement as separate compensation would need a further proof. [Passive-corner note, §3; reserve note, §§1–3.]7. The AA no-passive10 implication uses the correct structural factFix a full endpoint component  $c$  satisfying the accepted nonexceptional AA hypotheses. Restrict the curve collection and all its counts to  $c$ .Let a phase10 owner lie in one of these closed specified components. Both of its specified outer-corner ports participate in neutral edges, so both original corner receivers are nonfull  $2P1T$ .Suppose one port were passive. By the occurrence inclusion above, it would be a  $B_c$  corner. The accepted AA theorem then forces the owner’s other original outer-corner receiver to be full. That contradicts the other port’s participation in a neutral edge.Therefore every phase10 owner in these closed components is double-active, and

The counting inequalities give

Thus  $q_{01}\ge2$  also forces at least two double-active phase01 owners, as claimed. In a mixed component with no passive10 ports, the balance instead is
